# 石油出口路線再受威脅，英債賣壓推升美債殖利率

## 能源風險從荷莫茲延伸至紅海

沙烏地另一條石油出口路線受威脅，加上英國公債大跌，提高了持有長天期債券的成本，美債回吐週五長端漲幅。10年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.60%，其中4個基點來自實質殖利率；30年期同樣上升5個基點至5.11%，2年期則小升3個基點至4.21%。

新的能源風險在紅海。伊朗支持的胡塞組織威脅沙烏地海上運輸，讓原本協助繞過荷莫茲受阻航道的替代路線也面臨危險。煉油限制早已使成品油相對原油維持高價，因此衝擊不只是油價又波動一天，而是汽油、柴油與運輸成本可能持續偏高。英國方面，首相安迪・伯納姆談及運用既有財政規則的彈性支應投資，也引發長天期英債賣壓。

壓力尚未造成風險資產全面撤退。高收益債基金幾乎持平，半導體股小幅回升，波動率下降。甲骨文債券卻繼續走擴，使上週降評成為持續的次級市場壓力，而更多AI相關供給又將到來。當天的對比，是主權融資成本提高、企業風險集中在特定發行人，並非整個市場立即缺乏現金。

## 實質殖利率回升，投資人重估等待的成本

沙烏地經紅海路線出口的原油，上月已達每日419萬桶紀錄。荷莫茲仍嚴重受阻時，這條通道再遭威脅，增加了出口與航運持續中斷的可能。問題不只在原油庫存多少，也在於能否運出去，以及能否加工成可使用的燃料。

3-2-1裂解價差接近多年高點$70，超過歷史平均6倍。美國汽油平均每加侖$4.60，一年前為$3.63。WTI上漲約0.90%至$83.23，布蘭特上漲1.27%至$89.22。這樣的煉油利潤意味著，即使原油回落，加油站價格也未必同幅下降，而家庭支出與通膨預期更直接受到後者影響。

6月通膨報告較溫和後，市場仍大致排除7月底升息25個基點的可能，但年底前計入34個基點升息，9月與10月都有一定機率行動。華許先前警告，一份良性的CPI並不代表通膨任務完成，對較後段政策路徑仍有意義。

DoubleLine的比爾・坎貝爾提出另一個央行可能等待的理由：美債殖利率偏高，本身已在收緊借款條件，若通膨繼續改善，政策利率便有空間維持不變。他也認為，石油供給衝擊反而值得保持耐心，因為升息無法補回失去的能源供應。這不等於燃料成本沒有危害，而是讓既有融資成本承擔更多抑制作用，而非立即再提高政策利率。

5年期美債殖利率上升5個基點至4.33%，與10年期、30年期升幅相同。曲線小幅趨陡，2s10s擴大2個基點至39個基點，2s30s擴大2個基點至90個基點。以一週來看，2年期、5年期、10年期仍分別低5、4、2個基點，30年期則高1個基點；一個月的比較對長端更不利，2年期上升2個基點，30年期上升21個基點。

10年期實質殖利率回到2.35%，損益兩平通膨率升1個基點至2.25%。5年期與7年期實質殖利率各升4個基點至2.05%、2.19%，20年期升3個基點至2.70%，30年期升4個基點至2.91%。油價使通膨補償增加，但名目殖利率上升的大部分，仍來自實質殖利率。

現金投資人選擇保留彈性，而不是撤回資金。管理超過$8兆的貨幣市場基金偏好幾週內到期、可續作或重設利率的工具。6月附買回配置增加約$360億至$1.89兆，美國公債浮動利率券持有量則達紀錄$5,230億。這些券能取得偏高的3個月短券利率，又不必鎖定較長固定利率存續期間。

聯邦住宅貸款銀行今年流通債務增加約$1,800億，其中約$1,400億為浮動利率發行；貨幣基金增加約$1,950億機構債曝險。週一極短天期短券殖利率持平或下降，較長短券則上升，52週券達4.03%。重設利率工具仍有需求，顯示現金沒有消失，只是投資人較不願意長時間鎖住固定利率。

## 甲骨文利差續擴，更多科技融資排隊進場

甲骨文5年期信用違約交換成本升至每年約203個基點，為可追溯至2008年底的紀錄高點。票息6.7%、2056年到期債券利差擴大約8個基點至263個基點，票息5.7%、2036年到期券擴大約9個基點至205個基點。標普先前已將公司降至非投資級之上一級，穆迪則維持Baa2、負向展望。週一新增的是現券市場壓力，而不是另一項降評。

身為美國高評級公司債指數最大非金融發行人，甲骨文已成為市場能容忍多少AI支出的重要觀察對象。增資或客戶預付款可以減輕壓力，但投資人仍需判斷擴張何時才能帶來現金。第二家評等機構尚未取消投資級、改變可投資買方範圍前，價格已經先行調整。

新供給沒有放緩。BlackRock正準備透過持股公司發行超過$120億債券，支應其在Meta艾爾帕索資料中心計畫的80%權益，Meta持有其餘20%。Amazon的$250億交易反應較淡、大型科技業5年債務翻倍之後，這筆計畫又將增加大額科技相關曝險，即使發行主體是專案持股公司，而非一般母公司債。

Netflix則是規模較小、近期用途較清楚的再融資。公司以初步美債加95個基點指引，推銷$10億2036年到期券，用於償還2026年稍後到期的約$10億債務及一般企業支出。其2056年到期債券交易價格約92.94美分，為一年來盤中低點。先前投資級發行曾吸引超過10倍訂單，新交易卻需面對成長放緩與更擁擠的發行日程。

公開投資級以外的資金仍可取得，只是價格高得多。Shapoorji Pallonji完成INR1,510億、折合$16億交易，為Goswami Infratech債務再融資。3年期零息盧比債殖利率18.95%，另外3年期美元債籌得$6.5億、殖利率14.5%。借款由Afcons Infrastructure與Tata Sons股權擔保，其中INR1,350億須在24個月內償還。這筆完成的融資同時包含高利率、擔保品與大額近期還款要求。

能源也正影響獲利與收購。油價及需求偏弱迫使Ryanair降低票價，季度獲利下降34%至€5.38億。公司已將截至3月的80%燃料，以每桶$67避險，剩餘20%則承受邊際價格。Magnolia Oil以$40.6億收購WildFire Energy，動用3,220萬股並承接$6億2029年到期債券。前者呈現營運成本避險的限制，後者則是產油商運用股權與承接債務擴張。

Oncoclinicas已從準備重整，進展到與部分債權人就BRL51億達成庭外協議。在巴西兩位數利率下，收購推高了槓桿。IG4尋求超過半數表決權，並提議以優先於其他債務的可轉債投入約BRL5億新資金。提案仍不具約束力，取決於排他安排與盡職調查，因此新資金順位仍須與既有債權人協商。

Alkegen則更進一步。這家特殊材料業者同意預先協商的Chapter 11程序，將減少約$31億債務，並取得$3.15億破產融資支應營運。99%第一順位貸款人及多數第二順位貸款人支持，降低了執行不確定性，但債轉股與破產融資優先權，仍會重新分配資本結構各層的價值。

主要基金變化遠小於個別發行人的調整。美債殖利率提高，LQD下跌約0.38%至107.15；HYG上升約0.04%至79.68，JNK下跌約0.03%至95.95。一般再融資、專案債及昂貴私人融資都還能進行，但槓桿、擔保品與順位決定了取得資金的價格和形式。

## 英國財政彈性，遇上真實的借款成本

英國10年期公債殖利率上升8個基點至5.03%，30年期升9個基點至5.75%，為5月20日以來最高。伯納姆表示將運用既有財政規則的彈性後，英鎊兌美元一度下跌0.3%。美債隨英債走低，投資人重新衡量承接長天期主權債所需的報酬。

伯納姆並未宣布放棄規則，也承諾交代支出資金來源。疑慮在於，擴張公營金融機構是否容許更多借款落在主要債務限制之外。Resolution Foundation提議向國家財富基金注入£160億，以吸引超過£400億私人共同投資，投入能源及基礎設施。財政分類或許能改變，債務卻仍需要買家與償付。

該機構估計，每多借£10億，就增加約£5,000萬年度利息。英國借款成本已居G10最高，公共債務又接近一年GDP，融資問題無法與投資目標分開。英鎊走弱，也沒有支持一個單純以未來成長改善為中心的市場解讀。

歐元區企業面對另一種限制。ECB第二季企業調查中，淨42%企業反映銀行貸款利率提高，高於第一季26%；淨31%反映其他融資成本增加，淨10%反映擔保要求提高。整體貸款可取得性大致穩定，但大型企業淨改善4%，中小企業淨惡化4%，融資缺口由2%擴大至3%。

淨29%企業認為經濟前景限制外部融資。在計畫投資AI的企業中，72%預期使用內部資金，銀行貸款、補助、租賃各約16%，只有1%預期使用債券。這些選擇顯示，即使貸款供應沒有全面崩落，借款成本提高仍能減緩投資，或改變資金組合。

對債市而言，英國財政計畫帶來眼前供給與利息成本疑慮，歐元區企業條件趨緊則指向日後民間需求放緩。週一市場反應以英債為主，但企業調查也支持另一個看法：高借款成本已在執行部分央行希望達到的抑制效果。

## 印尼匯率回穩，仍仰賴代價不低的政策支撐

EMB下跌約0.17%至95.37，美元指數上升約0.24%至100.99。較高美國實質殖利率與較強美元是共同逆風，但印尼顯示，本地政策仍可維持國內債券需求。

印尼盾自18,190兌$1的紀錄低點回升約1.3%，前一收盤為17,895；3個月隱含波動率由7.93%降至6.78%。印尼央行2026年已累計升息100個基點，並收緊投機資金流動規範，協助穩定匯率，代價則是國內融資仍昂貴。

10年期政府債殖利率約7.25%，外資可望連續第二個月淨買進。標普7月13日確認投資級評等與展望，仍是支撐基礎。分析師預期財政赤字低於GDP的3%，政府與央行協調能否維持信心，對資金持續流入很重要。

油價使這個平衡更難維持。能源上漲提高家庭補貼成本，對經常帳赤字國家也形成壓力，使政府在捍衛貨幣時，更缺乏支持活動的空間。高殖利率既吸引買盤，也反映穩定資產所需的政策努力。週一外部環境提高了門檻，但尚未抹去已經實現的波動率改善。

## 股市比債市更有支撐

S&P 500下跌約0.19%至7,443.28，Nasdaq 100小漲約0.04%至28,604.23，半導體指數上升約0.60%至11,743.85，VIX下降約0.64%至18.65。多數個股走弱，但科技反彈與波動率降低，不像無差別的風險資產出清。

相較先前跌幅，反彈仍小。半導體一週仍跌約4.89%，一個月跌18.11%；Nasdaq 100一個月跌約5.93%。AI收入何時到位的問題，沒有隨一天反彈消失，甲骨文利差與即將到來的融資日程就是例子。

衝突再起，黃金期貨仍下跌約0.06%至$4,010.30，美元與實質殖利率則提高。油價是連結燃料成本、政策預期及能源進口國的共同不利因素，但資產間傳導仍不均衡。在高收益債基金或股市波動尚未顯示全面撤退之前，固定收益已先承受較高實質融資成本。

## 接下來測試更高殖利率是否足以吸引買盤

7月23日美東13:00將標售$210億新10年期TIPS，7月31日交割、2036年7月15日到期；6月新屋銷售於7月24日10:00公布。標售需求與其後實質殖利率走勢，將顯示跌價是否已吸引買家，房屋銷售則提供高借款成本抑制需求的證據。若油價使通膨補償居高不下，兩者互動比任何單項結果更重要。

歐元區銀行放款調查於7月21日美東04:00公布，英國零售銷售在7月24日02:00。兩者將補充民間需求是否已弱到足以抵銷歐洲債市面對的通膨與財政壓力。日本6月全國CPI於美東7月23日19:30、即當地7月24日公布，影響日本公債殖利率預期及海外債券的相對吸引力。

信用市場有更直接的需求測試。穆迪將Aa1展望調整為穩定後，華盛頓特區$12億所得稅擔保債預計7月21日定價。Netflix最終條件，以及超過$120億、與Meta相關的艾爾帕索融資計畫，將顯示不同借款人如何在同一個高利率市場成交。尤其甲骨文仍在重新定價，訂單、最終讓步與次級市場表現，會比待發行規模本身更有資訊價值。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil-route threats and a gilt selloff push Treasury yields higher

## Energy pressure spreads beyond Hormuz

Treasuries gave back Friday's long-end rally as threats to another Saudi oil-export route and a sharp gilt selloff raised the cost of holding duration. The 10-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.60%, with 4 basis points coming from its real component. The 30-year also rose 5 basis points, to 5.11%, while the 2-year increased a smaller 3 to 4.21%.

The new energy risk was in the Red Sea. Iran-backed Houthis threatened maritime traffic from Saudi Arabia, endangering a route that had helped bypass the disruption in Hormuz. Refining constraints were already keeping fuel prices high relative to crude, so the threat extended beyond another volatile oil session to the cost of gasoline, diesel and transport. In Britain, investors also sold long gilts after Prime Minister Andy Burnham discussed using flexibility within existing fiscal rules to finance investment.

The pressure did not produce a broad retreat from risk. High-yield funds were almost flat, semiconductor shares recovered slightly and volatility eased. Oracle's bonds nevertheless widened further, turning last week's downgrade into a continuing secondary-market problem as more AI-linked supply approached. The contrast was between higher sovereign financing costs and selective corporate strain, rather than an immediate shortage of cash across markets.

## Real yields rise as investors reassess the cost of waiting

Saudi exports through the Red Sea route had reached a record 4.19 million barrels a day in the previous month. Threatening that corridor while Hormuz remained heavily impaired raised the possibility of more persistent export and shipping disruption. The risk was not confined to the level of crude inventories: transport access and the ability to turn crude into usable fuel also mattered.

The 3-2-1 crack spread was near a multiyear high of $70, more than six times its historical average. US gasoline averaged $4.60 a gallon, against $3.63 a year earlier. WTI rose about 0.90% to $83.23 and Brent 1.27% to $89.22. Those refining margins meant that a decline in crude would not necessarily deliver equivalent relief at the pump, where fuel costs affect household spending and inflation expectations more directly.

Markets still largely discounted a quarter-point Fed increase at the end of July after the softer June inflation reports. But year-end pricing carried 34 basis points of tightening, with meaningful odds of action in September and October. Kevin Warsh's warning that one benign CPI reading did not finish the inflation task remained relevant to that later path.

DoubleLine's Bill Campbell offered a reason the Fed might nevertheless wait. Elevated Treasury yields were already tightening borrowing conditions, he argued, and could allow policy rates to remain unchanged if inflation continued to moderate. He also saw an oil supply shock as a reason for patience: higher rates cannot restore missing energy supply. That view differs from assuming fuel costs are harmless; it places more of the restraint on existing borrowing costs rather than another immediate policy increase.

The 5-year Treasury yield rose 5 basis points to 4.33%, matching the increases at ten and 30 years. The curve steepened modestly, with 2s10s widening 2 basis points to 39 and 2s30s widening 2 to 90. Over the week, 2-, 5- and 10-year yields were still lower by 5, 4 and 2 basis points, while the 30-year was up 1. The monthly comparison was much less favorable to the long end: increases ranged from 2 basis points at two years to 21 at 30 years.

The 10-year real yield returned to 2.35%, while its breakeven rose 1 basis point to 2.25%. Five- and seven-year real yields each increased 4 basis points to 2.05% and 2.19%; the 20-year rose 3 to 2.70%, and the 30-year 4 to 2.91%. Inflation compensation responded to oil, but real-yield increases accounted for most of the nominal selloff.

Cash investors were preserving flexibility rather than withdrawing funds. Money-market funds overseeing more than $8 trillion favored securities that mature, roll or reset within weeks. Their repo allocations increased about $36 billion in June to roughly $1.89 trillion, while Treasury floating-rate-note holdings reached a record $523 billion. Those notes allowed exposure to elevated 3-month bill rates without locking in longer fixed-rate duration.

Federal Home Loan Bank debt outstanding had increased about $180 billion during the year, including roughly $140 billion of floating-rate issuance; money funds added about $195 billion of agency exposure. Very short bill yields were stable to lower on Monday, while longer bills firmed, with the 52-week yield at 4.03%. The demand for resettable claims showed how cash remained available even as investors became reluctant to commit to a fixed rate for longer.

## Oracle widens further as more technology financing approaches

Oracle's 5-year default-protection cost reached about 203 basis points annually, the highest in a history extending to late 2008. The spread on its 6.7% bond due 2056 widened about 8 basis points to 263; its 5.7% note due 2036 widened roughly 9 to 205. S&P had already cut the company to one notch above speculative grade, while Moody's maintained Baa2 with a negative outlook. Monday added fresh cash-market evidence to the rating concern rather than another downgrade.

As the largest nonfinancial issuer in the US high-grade corporate index, Oracle had become a prominent measure of the market's tolerance for AI spending. Equity financing or customer prepayments could reduce pressure, but investors still needed to judge when the expansion would generate cash. Prices were adjusting before any second agency removed investment-grade status and potentially changed the eligible buyer base.

New supply was not slowing. BlackRock was preparing more than $12 billion of bonds through the holding company for its 80% interest in a Meta data-center project in El Paso; Meta owns the remaining 20%. After the subdued reception for Amazon's $25 billion deal and Big Tech's doubling of debt over five years, the proposed transaction would add another large technology-linked exposure, even though it used a project holding company rather than a conventional parent-company bond.

Netflix offered a smaller refinancing with a clearer near-term use of proceeds. It marketed $1 billion of 2036 notes at initial guidance of 95 basis points over Treasuries, intending to repay roughly $1 billion due later in 2026 and fund corporate expenses. Its 2056 bonds traded near 92.94 cents, the lowest intraday price in a year. A previous investment-grade sale had attracted orders above ten times its size; the new deal faced slower growth and a more crowded calendar.

Outside public investment grade, funding was available at a much higher price. Shapoorji Pallonji completed an INR151 billion, or $1.6 billion, transaction to refinance Goswami Infratech debt. Three-year zero-coupon rupee bonds yielded 18.95%, while a separate three-year dollar bond raised $650 million at 14.5%. Afcons Infrastructure and Tata Sons shares backed the borrowings, and INR135 billion had to be repaid within 24 months. The completed financing combined high yields, collateral and a substantial near-term repayment requirement.

Energy was also affecting earnings and acquisitions. Ryanair's quarterly profit fell 34% to €538 million as oil costs and softer demand forced fare reductions. It had hedged 80% of fuel at $67 a barrel through March, leaving the remaining 20% exposed to the marginal price. Magnolia Oil's $4.06 billion acquisition of WildFire Energy used 32.2 million shares and assumed $600 million of notes due in 2029. One case showed the limits of hedging operating costs; the other showed a producer using equity and assumed debt to expand.

Oncoclinicas had moved from preparing a restructuring to agreeing with part of its creditor group on an out-of-court deal covering BRL5.1 billion. Acquisitions had increased leverage under double-digit Brazilian interest rates. IG4 sought more than half the voting rights and proposed about BRL500 million of new capital through convertible bonds ranking ahead of other debt. The offer remained nonbinding, subject to exclusivity and due diligence, leaving the proposed priority to be negotiated with existing creditors.

Alkegen was further along. The specialty-materials producer agreed to a prepackaged Chapter 11 process that would cut about $3.1 billion of debt and provide a $315 million bankruptcy loan for operations. Support from 99% of first-lien lenders and a majority of second-lien lenders reduced uncertainty over execution, although the debt-for-equity exchange and debtor-in-possession priority still redistributed value across the capital structure.

The broad fund moves were far smaller than these issuer-level adjustments. LQD fell about 0.38% to 107.15 as Treasury yields rose, while HYG gained about 0.04% to 79.68 and JNK slipped about 0.03% to 95.95. Routine refinancing, project debt and expensive private funding could all proceed, but leverage, collateral and priority determined the price and form of that access.

## Britain's fiscal flexibility runs into the cost of borrowing

UK 10-year gilt yields rose 8 basis points to 5.03%, while 30-year yields climbed 9 to 5.75%, their highest since May 20. Sterling fell as much as 0.3% against the dollar after Burnham said the government would use available flexibility within existing fiscal rules. Treasuries declined alongside gilts as investors reassessed the compensation required to absorb long sovereign debt.

Burnham had not announced an abandonment of the rules and pledged to explain how spending would be funded. The concern was instead whether expanding public financial institutions would allow more borrowing outside the main debt constraint. The Resolution Foundation proposed a £16 billion injection into the National Wealth Fund to attract more than £40 billion of private co-investment in energy and infrastructure. The fiscal classification might change, but the debt would still need buyers and servicing.

Resolution estimated that each extra £1 billion borrowed would add about £50 million of annual interest. With UK borrowing costs already the highest in the G10 and public debt around annual GDP, the financing question could not be separated from the investment ambition. Sterling's decline offered little support for an interpretation centered solely on stronger future growth.

Euro-area companies faced a different constraint. In the ECB's second-quarter firm survey, a net 42% reported higher bank-loan interest rates, up from 26% in the first quarter. Net shares of 31% and 10% reported higher other financing costs and collateral requirements. Overall loan availability was broadly steady, but improved by a net 4% for large firms and deteriorated by a net 4% for small and medium-sized businesses. The financing gap widened to 3% from 2%.

A net 29% cited the economic outlook as a constraint on external finance. Among firms planning AI investment, 72% expected to use internal funds, around 16% each named bank loans, grants or leasing, and only 1% expected to use debt securities. These financing choices showed how higher borrowing costs could slow or reshape investment without an outright collapse in loan availability.

The contrast matters for duration. UK fiscal plans raised an immediate supply and interest-cost concern, while tighter euro-area corporate terms pointed toward slower private demand over time. Monday's market response was dominated by the gilt channel, but the survey supported the argument that high borrowing costs were already doing part of central banks' work.

## Indonesia's currency recovery still depends on costly policy support

EMB fell about 0.17% to 95.37 as the dollar index rose about 0.24% to 100.99. Higher US real yields and a firmer dollar were common headwinds, but Indonesia illustrated how local policy could still sustain demand for domestic bonds.

The rupiah had recovered about 1.3% from its record low of 18,190 per dollar to a prior close of 17,895. Three-month implied volatility fell to 6.78% from 7.93%. Bank Indonesia had raised rates by a cumulative 100 basis points during 2026 and tightened rules on speculative flows, helping stabilize the currency at the cost of maintaining expensive domestic funding.

The 10-year government bond offered about 7.25%, and foreigners were on course for a second consecutive month of net purchases. S&P's July 13 affirmation of the investment-grade rating and outlook remained a supporting baseline. Analysts expected the fiscal deficit below 3% of GDP, with confidence in government-central-bank coordination important to continued inflows.

Oil made that balance harder to maintain. Higher prices increased the cost of household subsidies and weighed on a country running a current-account deficit, reducing the room to support activity while defending the currency. The high yield was both an attraction to buyers and a reflection of the policy effort required to stabilize assets. Monday's external move raised that hurdle without erasing the improvement in volatility already achieved.

## Equities hold up better than bonds

The S&P 500 slipped about 0.19% to 7,443.28, while the Nasdaq 100 edged up about 0.04% to 28,604.23 and the semiconductor index gained about 0.60% to 11,743.85. VIX eased about 0.64% to 18.65. Most shares weakened, but the technology rebound and lower volatility did not resemble indiscriminate risk liquidation.

The recovery was small relative to prior losses. Semiconductors remained down about 4.89% over the week and 18.11% over the month; the Nasdaq 100 was about 5.93% lower over the month. Questions about the timing of AI revenue had not disappeared with a one-day bounce, as Oracle's widening spreads and the approaching financing calendar demonstrated.

Gold futures slipped about 0.06% to $4,010.30 despite the renewed conflict, while the dollar and real yields rose. Oil was the shared adverse development linking fuel costs, policy expectations and energy-importing sovereigns, but its transmission across assets remained uneven. Fixed income absorbed higher real financing costs before there was evidence of a broader retreat in high-yield funds or equity volatility.

## Supply and demand will test whether higher yields are enough

The $21 billion new 10-year TIPS auction on July 23 at 13:00 ET settles July 31 and matures July 15, 2036. June new-home sales follow July 24 at 10:00. Auction demand and subsequent real-yield trading will show whether the selloff has attracted buyers, while home sales will provide evidence of the restraint imposed by high borrowing costs. The interaction matters more than either release alone if oil keeps inflation compensation elevated.

The euro-area bank lending survey is due July 21 at 04:00 ET, followed by UK retail sales July 24 at 02:00. They will add evidence on whether private demand is weakening enough to offset the inflation and fiscal pressures weighing on European bonds. Japan's June national CPI arrives July 23 at 19:30 ET, corresponding to the July 24 local release, and will inform expectations for JGB yields and the relative appeal of foreign bonds.

Credit offers several direct demand tests. The District of Columbia's $1.2 billion income-tax-backed sale is expected July 21 after Moody's stabilized its Aa1 outlook. Netflix's final terms and the planned Meta-linked El Paso financing of more than $12 billion will show how different borrowers clear the same higher-rate market. Orders, final concessions and secondary performance will be more informative than pipeline size alone, particularly alongside Oracle's continuing repricing.
